unprobeable.codebuddy: CodeBuddy signs in against Tencent’s own service, so its key can’t be checked from here — save it and launch the agent to verify. Note that CODEBUDDY_BASE_URL selects another CodeBuddy deployment (enterprise or self-hosted), not an OpenAI-compatible endpoint: a model-gateway or relay key won’t work with this agent.
unprobeable.cursor: Cursor signs in through its own service — there’s no key endpoint to test here. Save the key and launch the agent to verify.
unprobeable.amp: Amp authenticates against Sourcegraph’s own service — its key is verified by running the CLI. Save it and launch the agent, or run `amp login`.
unprobeable.commandcode: Command Code verifies its key against its own account service — there’s no endpoint to test here. Save it and launch the agent, or run `command-code login`.
unprobeable.copilot: Copilot authenticates with your GitHub account, and its token is checked by GitHub on first use — there’s no model endpoint to probe here. Save it and launch the agent to verify.
unprobeable.claudeOauth: A subscription token is verified by Claude itself on first use — there’s no endpoint to test it against here. Save it and send a message in the workspace to confirm.
unprobeable.aider: Aider injects your key into the provider chosen by AIDER_PROVIDER (or the model name) and verifies it on its first run — there’s no single endpoint to test here. Set AIDER_PROVIDER (and LLM_BASE_URL for a relay) to have it checked, or save and send a message in the workspace to confirm.
unprobeable.cline: Cline targets your selected provider — this provider can’t be tested directly here. Save the settings and launch the agent to verify (or run `cline auth`).

endpointMismatch.gatewayIntoPlatform: That looks like a model API endpoint (an OpenAI-compatible gateway or relay). This agent cannot use one: this field takes a deployment of the vendor’s own service. For a model-gateway key, use an OpenAI-protocol agent such as opencode, openclaw or codex.

noEndpoint.commandcode: Command Code configures its own BYOK providers in ~/.commandcode/providers.json and calls them straight from this machine, so there is no endpoint field here. Once one is set up, name the model as provider/model above — for example openrouter/deepseek-v4-flash.
noEndpoint.cline: Cline’s providers and their endpoints are set up by `cline auth`, so there is no endpoint field here. The provider above only picks among the ones already configured.
noEndpoint.cursor: Cursor authenticates against its own service and takes no custom endpoint, so there is no such field here.
noEndpoint.copilot: Copilot uses your GitHub account and GitHub decides the endpoint, so there is no endpoint field here.
